checks: The statements explicitly override the commutative convention only for the two new lemmas and use associative unital rings, unital left modules, and the finite stabilizer H=G_x.
The degree-zero comparison is only an isomorphism of abelian groups; no natural left-R module structure on noncommutative internal Hom is asserted.
Local finite presentation of the first Hom argument identifies the internal-Hom stalk with Hom over R_x, and H-fixed maps are exactly U_x-linear maps.
Because H is finite, U_x is finite free as a left R_x-module; left Noetherianity of R_x therefore makes U_x left Noetherian.
The equivariant local generator L(T)=Ind_G(j_{T!}R|T) has stalk U_x. The h-summand map is m to rho^R_{h,x}(m)[h], with the semilinear coefficient action and left multiplication on [h].

For left generators a_i of a left ideal, the stalk map is (u_i) to sum u_i a_i. Right multiplication by each chosen generator is the correct orientation for a left U_x-linear map from the free left module.
The local image is finitely presented under the stated left-coherence hypothesis, so the degree-zero comparison represents the Baer map on an orbit neighbourhood.
Equivariant extension by zero is exact and left adjoint to restriction; injectivity extends the represented ideal map to U_x, proving left injectivity by the left Baer criterion.
An equivariant injective resolution remains an injective U_x-resolution after taking the stalk, and the termwise Hom comparison gives the all-degree Ext comparison.
In the commutative case, forgetting the module structure on equivariant SheafExt is exact and both derived functors use the same injective resolution.
The local fixed-point hypotheses strictly strengthen the source's global coherent-R, coherent-A, and left-Noetherian-stalk formulation.
No whole-group G skew ring, right-module, two-sided-ideal, semisimplicity, stabilizer-order inversion, free-action, or unrestricted stalk-preservation claim is made.
